newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran, Turkey, Turkmenistan ministers meet on gas.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Turkey, Turkmenistan ministers meet on gas.

text.p: Ministers from Iran, Turkey and Turkmenistan discussed gas exports to Turkey and other energy projects during a meeting in Tehran on Saturday, Iran's state-run radio said.
"The trilateral ministerial meeting reviewed Iran's and Turkmenistan's gas exports to Turkey," the radio said.
It quoted Gholamreza Aghazadeh, Iran's oil minister, as saying that cooperation among the three countries "could be a model for regional economic cooperation."
He said that the low cost of exporting gas to Turkey would benefit the three countries.
Aghazadeh said that from 1998 gas exports to Turkey would initially be about four billion cubic metres from Iran and two billion cubic metres from Turkmenistan.

Turkey signed a landmark 23-year, $23 billion agreement with Iran in August to buy an initial three billion cubic metres of gas a year from 1998 through a pipeline to built by Turkey and Iran on their own territories.
A statement by the Turkish energy ministry on Friday said the talks were expected to focus on a multi-billion dollar deal to carry Turkmen gas to Turkey and Europe through a pipeline.

The pipeline project was proposed in 1995 but later dropped due to financial difficulties and U.S. reservations over Iran's involvement. A revised project proposes a new 400-km (250 mile) Turkish line bypassing Iran.
